judgements.justification: A's capacity concern was closed by a new table and its champion rose to 8, while B's objection that XML uses two fixed roles is structural, so B's rebuttal moved one reviewer by one point.
Without Reviewer_sKB5's 8, the only rating above 7 in either committee, A's remaining scores (7, 6, 7) equal B's exactly, and the 8 lifted A's mean to 7.0 for the spotlight.
A's outlier, Reviewer_sKB5, engaged with the rebuttal and rose on it; the silent Reviewer_rafZ was not an outlier.
Neither area chair set aside a low outlying score; B has no detractor below 6.
B's reservation was that the XML task does not exercise HRR binding, not that the paper is too specialised for the audience; A's area chair called it of broad interest.
A's 'all reviewers much more confident' overstates, but three of four reviewers did raise their scores, so the spotlight rests on the real final scores, not on the overstatement.
Two of B's three reviewers replied to the response and one rose; in A one reviewer was silent, so neither committee had most reviewers ignore the rebuttal.
A's non-expert Reviewer_m8WY gave 7, but removing it would raise A's mean (8, 7, 7), so it did not lift A above its checked assessments.
No committee split evenly between accept and reject; all seven final ratings are 6 or above.
The responses answered different questions (a capacity table for A, promised text and an example for B) and did not conflict; no result or account differed between committees.
Reviewer_rafZ flagged the omitted Plate prior work, and the unchallenged 'first' claim stood equally before both committees, so it fed no difference.
A's spotlight follows a 7.0 mean with an 8, and its meta-review states grounds (future work, broad interest).
B's critics were HRR-literate reviewers objecting to the demonstration task, not to the paper's framing from a neighbouring field.
B's most positive reviewer, Reviewer_uoCQ, engaged with the rebuttal and rose to 7, so B did not lack an engaged supporter.
Neither committee rejected the paper or called the promised revisions too large for camera-ready.
Both meta-reviews draw only on their own reviewers' text; no off-record input appears.
B required the method to show usefulness on a task that tests compositional binding and held this against it, while A valued the trainable-HRR step on its own terms.
No reviewer held a below-threshold score after the rebuttal; the lowest final ratings are 6.
